id: AT-RN-06 (HOME-GUARD: no case reaches the real home)
note: HOME-GUARD (0.1.2): a kit test elsewhere ran a planted hook with the real HOME and wiped ~/.claude/settings.json; the settings writer (lib/settings_write.pm) writes ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json, and the helper writes its handoff root and watch logs under $XDG_STATE_HOME, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and the folder options. Inside a case the runner's own HOME is the case's $HOME and no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE*, XDG_* or GIT_* name is set (the runner drops the caller's at start). With stand-ins for the real HOME, the account's home, the config folder and the state folders given (all under $TMP: no link into the real home is made), home_guard refuses, before the fork, a helper call or command whose HOME is a real home (by real path or device and inode: a link to it, or another case of its name), missing, empty, relative or outside the temp folders (also in a folder whose name a temp folder's begins), whose HOME or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR has a `..` part (the kernel applies it after links: $TMP/L/.. with L a link into the real home is the real home), whose CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is a real config folder (also when TMPDIR is the home or another case of it) or not under a temp folder, whose config folder (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else $HOME/.claude) or its settings.json leads by real path to a real config folder or outside temp, or is a dangling link (links inside temp are taken), whose $HOME/.local, .local/state, .local/share, .cache or .config is a dangling link or leads by real path to a real config or state folder or outside temp, with a link at any depth below HOME, the config folder or a state folder that leads (dangling or not, also through a temp folder it links to) to a real home, into a real config or state folder or outside temp (the link walk; past its entry or depth budget, or a folder the guard cannot list but a child can go through, is refused too), whose XDG_STATE_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, folder option or CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR is outside temp, relative (an option), through `..`, or in a real config or state folder, and a declared builtin home at the account's home; a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under temp outside HOME is walked too, and XDG_DATA_HOME is read as a state folder. With a temp HOME whose .claude links to the stand-in real one, the runner's own options write and a setup write are refused before they write, and a builtin run after a setup link into the stand-in real .local/state is refused. A child run of the runner over two case-local cases (a helper call with no HOME; one with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR outside the temp folders) fails both with the guard's line; a child run started with the state folders, the helper's STORE_TEST_TRACE and STORE_TEST_MODE and the shell start-up files (BASH_ENV, ENV, ZDOTDIR) at stand-ins passes none of them to its case, and nothing lands there; a child run started with GIT_DIR at a stand-in repo passes it to no fixture git command (its case's repo gets the commits, the stand-in keeps its one); a child run whose TMPDIR lies in a stand-in real config folder, or in a stand-in state folder given, one whose --repo-tmp folder lies in a stand-in real state folder, one whose TMPDIR is relative, one whose TMPDIR goes through a link into a stand-in real config folder and `..`, one whose TMPDIR is a stand-in real home, one whose --repo-tmp folder holds one outside the temp folders, and one started with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ~/cfg (read as the home's cfg) whose TMPDIR lies in that folder end at start, exit 2, with the guard's line, and nothing is written there; one whose TMPDIR lies under the stand-in home outside its config and state folders runs, and so does one whose HOME was made in its TMPDIR (as mktemp -d makes one under TMPDIR on macOS: a HOME given that is not the account's home and lies under a temp folder is a throwaway one), with nothing written in that HOME. At start a TMPDIR that holds a HOME given made in it is taken, and one at that HOME, at or above the account's home (also under the start TMPDIR, also by another case of its or its parent's name where the file system folds case) or at / is refused
